llm.summary: The skill is a legitimate Chinese-language storyboard helper, but its persistent learning feature can turn untrusted project data into instructions the agent is told to obey.

dimensions.detail: Reading user-selected article/storyboard files is proportionate, but reading .avs/learnings.jsonl from the current project and ~/.workbuddy/avs/learnings.jsonl by default broadens trust to local state that may not be user-reviewed.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The artifact is a static skill package with local Python scripts and markdown references; I found no dependency install step, network retrieval, remote execution, tool spoofing, or hidden install persistence.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md requires running learn.py digest before work and says every output entry must be followed, while learn.py prints free-form project and global learning text without schema validation or instruction/data separation.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill mandates writing two or three learning entries after each task and supports promoting project entries to global cross-project memory, creating persistent free-form influence over future agent behavior.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The files coherently support article-to-video storyboard drafting, scaffolding, validation, and learning; the marketing wording overstates automation somewhat, but the core behavior matches the stated workflow.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review this skill before installing if you work in shared or untrusted repositories. Do not let it blindly obey digest output from .avs/learnings.jsonl, and review any project learning entry before adding or promoting it to global memory. It is best suited for users who want a Chinese-first storyboard workflow and are comfortable with local persistent preference files.
llm.findings:
[T01] unexpected: The static finding is supported: project-controlled .avs/learnings.jsonl entries are loaded and printed by digest, and SKILL.md tells the agent to obey every entry. This is a prompt-injection and persistence concern, though the code does not directly execute those entries.
[LP3] expected: Local file reads/writes and learning storage are part of the stated purpose, but the required read/write workflow is under-scoped and lacks clear confirmation before persistent memory updates.
[TP4] expected: I downgraded this concern: the scripts alone do not fully generate a finished storyboard, but SKILL.md is an agent workflow where the model writes the missing content and the scripts provide scaffolding and checking.
[SQP-3] expected: The skill is clearly built for Chinese-language storyboard workflows and bilingual video prompts. This is a usability and disclosure limitation, not evidence of malicious or deceptive behavior.
[SDI-1] expected: storyboard_lib.py loading persistent avoid words is disclosed as the E8 learning-based check; the risk comes from free-form persistence and trust boundaries, not from the validation helper itself.
